what_it_does: Supercomputer centers historically run long-running batch jobs (high-performance computing workloads), but modern AI and interactive jobs have different requirements—they need quick response times and work poorly when queued behind month-long simulations. This paper proposes a scheduling strategy using Slurm (the standard job scheduler) that allows both batch HPC and interactive AI workloads to coexist on the same hardware by keeping all jobs short-lived and prioritizing interactive work.
